skills/make-it-so/playbooks/orchestrate..why: The orch CLI is excluded and the verification ledger lives in GitHub: every orch command becomes a direct store-file edit or a ledger comment on the PR, the store moves to ~/.claude/projects/<project>/, and restacks and cloud-only spawns become background agents with worktree isolation. The orch frontier command's empty-gt guard becomes an instruction. Worktree agents share one repository, so workers release their branches and the stacker frees held branches before a restack. Every agent runs on this machine, so the isolation exception covers only the coordinator's own working tree and worktree agents may read the store. The different-family verifier resolves to the models document's verifier and verifier-diff-audit roles, with a fallback line when there is no second family. Kitchen: every landing passes Autopilot-full's merge gate, and a closed gate parks in gates.md for the chef; human-in-the-loop units become local Projects threads running visual-grilling, with plain-text grilling as the fallback; a marker sentence says the Projects coordinator plus routines replace the /loop wakes. The reflect step that the substitution table appends to every playbook is carried by hand, since forks don't pick up rewrites.

skills/make-it-so/SKILL.md.why: Router: renamed make-it-so and made the kitchen's entry point, reached through the root AGENTS.md line, so the sticky-mode frontmatter (mode, icon, color, reminder) goes and the description says when to route. Routing rule: running something can answer it -> prototype; a one-way door or taste, intent or domain words only the chef holds -> grill, visual-grilling first; bigger than one context -> wayfinder; human-in-the-loop work runs as a local Projects thread with a plain-text fallback. Overlap wiring: Matt's implement, tdd, diagnosing-bugs, code-review, prototype and grilling are the procedures for their jobs; tdd-bug-fix stays for bugs, interrogate for one-way doors, and the Spec and tickets playbook is listed. Every playbook ends with Reflect. Autonomy: merges follow the trust ladder's merge gate, and one-way doors always wait for the chef. Model-invocable: milliways:poteto-agent preloads it, and Claude Code cannot preload a skill with model invocation off. Roles: the Subagents defaults resolve from docs/agents/models.md (written by setup-milliways) instead of setup-pstack and Cursor model slugs. Leaf skills: says where principle leaves and this skill's own files live (<milliways>), since Claude Code does not list skills with model invocation off.

skills/pr/SKILL.md.why: PR anatomy: keeps Summary, Evidence and Merge Danger, and adds a conventional-commit title, a calldiff call-tree summary sanity-checked for dynamic dispatch (Mermaid as fallback), a scope line, before/after media attached with gh --attach, the red-then-green test, a Blast radius: high|medium|low line with the one fact it is safe because of, the door:one-way label, commits regrouped in dependency order, the verifier verdict at the head SHA with its tier label, a decision-log link and the Fix-forward: #N line, which the trust-ladder scorer reads. One concern per PR, no stacks. Adds the Prototype PRs variant: a draft titled prototype: with a screencast per variant, closed unmerged with the chef's pick recorded on the PR and the ticket.

skills/make-it-so/playbooks/autopilot-fu.why: Merge gate (spec #66, trust ladder): the owner merges only when the PR's area is gated in docs/agents/autonomy.md (first matching Areas row per path, lowest rung across areas), CI is green, a fresh verifier passed at the head SHA and patch-id with the live lane as the floor, and the door is two-way (no door:one-way label, no path or change on the One-way doors list). Otherwise it stops at merge-ready for the chef; the operator's grant no longer opens a closed gate. A marker sentence says the Projects coordinator plus routines replace the hourly /loop tick.

skills/make-it-so/playbooks/bug-fix.md.why: Overlap: Matt's diagnosing-bugs is the kitchen's diagnosis procedure, so steps 1 and 2 run its loop (the repro is its feedback loop, the binary search its hypothesis phases) while keeping pstack's surface and evidence rules; tdd-bug-fix stays at step 5. Matt's code-review reviews the branch before Opening a PR.

skills/make-it-so/playbooks/feature.md.why: Overlap, in the spec's order prototype -> architect -> implement and tdd -> verify -> pr: a prototype step (Matt's prototype skill, or a winning prototype branch checked out as the reference spec and rebuilt on the paved path) before architect; the code delegate runs Matt's implement test-first with Matt's tdd; verify names the live-lane floor; Matt's code-review reviews every change, with interrogate kept for one-way doors and contested designs; Opening a PR writes the PR with the pr skill. Follow-ups get their own PRs, since the kitchen does not stack.

skills/make-it-so/playbooks/opening-a-pr.why: The pr skill owns the PR anatomy (title, body sections, evidence, labels), so pstack's Titles and Descriptions rules give way to it; one concern per PR with no stacks, except for a playbook the chef chose that delivers one; a prototype: PR is the one draft; Matt's code-review runs before every PR, and interrogate only for one-way doors.

skills/make-it-so/playbooks/prototype.md.why: Overlap: Matt's prototype skill builds the prototype. Prototype-as-spec: a choice for the chef ships as a draft prototype: PR with the prototype label and one screencast per variant, the chef picks by commenting, the PR closes unmerged with the decision recorded, and the kept branch is the build thread's reference spec, rebuilt on the paved path by Feature. A fork inside the thread's own task is decided from the evidence without a PR.

skills/make-it-so/playbooks/spec-and-tic.why: Port-only playbook, not in pstack: large or one-way-door work runs grill-with-docs (visual-grilling first), interrogate for a one-way door, to-spec, then to-tickets, per the spec's overlap table, and hands each ticket to its own playbook.
